title: VaLUH: Fast Algorithms for the Configuration Model of Vertex-Labeled Undirected Hypergraphs

problem.claim: Uniformly sample non-degenerate, vertex-labeled, undirected hypergraphs with prescribed vertex degrees and hyperedge sizes.

gap.claim: Existing approaches require more Markov-chain steps or more wall-clock time than the presented methods.

contributions.claim: VaLUH provides a suite of Markov-Chain-Monte-Carlo algorithms for the hypergraph micro-canonical configuration model.
The suite includes algorithms based on stub-labeled hypergraphs, edge-labeled hypergraphs, and direct sampling of vertex-labeled hypergraphs.
The algorithms define the Markov-chain state space graph and optimize transition probabilities using the Metropolis-Hastings approach.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors theoretically report that their algorithms require as many or fewer steps to converge to the stationary distribution than existing algorithms.
On real networks, the authors report that their methods are up to 6x faster than existing approaches in both number of steps and wall-clock time.
The authors report that the direct algorithm is the fastest and that the methods require less computation per step.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper addresses uniform sampling of constrained vertex-labeled undirected hypergraphs.
It presents three MCMC algorithms based on different labeling representations, including direct vertex-labeled sampling.
The authors theoretically relate the algorithms' convergence-step requirements to Peskun ordering.
The reported improvement comes from state-space graph design and Metropolis-Hastings transition-probability optimization.
Experiments on real networks report speedups of up to 6x, with the direct algorithm fastest.

source_observation.claim: The authors connect convergence efficiency to both state-space graph design and transition-probability optimization.

interpretation.claim: For MCMC algorithm design, improving the chain's ordering and proposal structure can matter alongside implementation-level optimization.

application.claim: When developing constrained sampling algorithms, evaluate both the induced state-space graph and the transition probabilities.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these design choices generalize beyond the stated hypergraph configuration-model setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact convergence criteria, state spaces, transition kernels, or theoretical assumptions.
The abstract does not provide datasets, experimental protocols, variance measures, or statistical uncertainty for the reported speedups.
